title: LumosAI PLG first-token pathway discussion
summary: Initial PLG/self-serve evaluation of Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Discussed quickstart, free credits, and time-to-first-token (TTFT). Clarified security requirements (SOC 2, SSO, KMS), pilot scope, and benchmarking needs. Agreed next steps: send playbook, security pack, and schedule a short bench run on hosted. Customer wants TTFT under 48 hours for dev team and pilot within 2 weeks.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit
Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, data residency
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Jenna, Marco (Redwood); Alice, Ben, Priya, Samir (LumosAI)

[00:00] Jenna (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick intro, i'm jenna, im the AE on this account, with marco our se, uh, can we do a quick round robin?
[00:12] Alice - LumosAI (CTO): hi all, Alice here, CTO at LumosAI. we run model-backed search and summarization in product. we're evaluating a few paths to get to first tokens fast.
[00:21] Ben (ML Eng): Ben — mainly curious about latency and cost, and how much work to switch models later.
[00:27] Marco (Redwood SE): great, thanks. quick note: we'll cover hosted api quickstart, reserved/dedicated options, and private v-p-c onprem style deployments. sorry, my mic fuzzed, i said V P C.
[00:39] Priya (Product): timeline is kind of tight — we'd like a dev-ready flow within 48 hours and a pilot in two weeks if everything looks good.
[00:46] Jenna: perfect. so quickstart — we give free credits for PLG signups, and a pre-built template for search summarization, that usually gets teams to first token in a few hours depending on infra.
[00:58] Alice: when you say "a few hours" — is that with existing infra or does someone need to spin up anything? we want minimal infra overhead.
[01:06] Marco: for the hosted api path nothing to spin up — it's just api keys, sdk, and you can stream responses. we can do a sandbox run that demonstrates typical latencies. sometimes transcription shows product names wrong, so sorry if i say "Redwood Dedicate" — i mean Redwood Dedicated.
[01:20] Ben: what's the typical token latency for our model sizes? we run 7B and 13B variants.
[01:27] Marco: for 7B on hosted we see p50 under 120ms for single-turn generation for short prompts, p95 around 300-600ms depending on sequence length. 13B adds ~2x. we'll share our perf spreadsheet.
[01:40] Samir (Infra): ok, security — we are SOC 2 Type II, need SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. can hosted satisfy that?
[01:49] Jenna: short answer: yes for most enterprise customers. Hosted supports SSO via SAML/Okta, audit logs, and we have KMS integrations for private deployments; for hosted there's a bring-your-key option via a managed HSM, and we can discuss ledger/audit export cadence. we'll send the security pack.
[02:05] Alice: data residency is a must for some EU customers, can we pin region?
[02:10] Marco: yes, hosted can be region pinned for EU; alternatively dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools in your region. Private is the on-prem route if you need full control.
[02:18] Priya: what's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated? rough order.
[02:22] Jenna: hosted is usage-based, so good for PLG and bursty traffic. Dedicated is committed monthly capacity — better unit economics at steady high throughput. we'll send a simple TCO sheet tailored to your expected volume.
[02:35] Ben: for a pilot we want to compare latency and cost more concretely. can we run a short benchmark?
[02:39] Marco: absolutely — we can run a 24-48 hour bench on hosted with your prompts to show p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost. note: our runtime does batching, KV cache — sometimes the transcriber writes that oddly as K-V cash — but that helps reduce per-token cost for repeated prefixes.
[02:55] Alice: great. what do we need from our side to get TTFT under 48 hours?
[03:00] Jenna: primarily, we need a dev contact to take API keys, a sample prompt set (5-10 prompts), and a small test dataset for embeddings if you use similarity. we'll also provision free credits.
[03:12] Priya: can our devs self-serve the whole thing or do we need a Redwood SE?
[03:17] Marco: most teams self-serve for basic flows. for the pilot bench and model selection we typically help — it's about a 30-60 minute pairing session to tune batching and quantization recommendations.
[03:29] Ben: are there any gotchas with model switch later? we might start with open weights then move to more tuned variants.
[03:35] Marco: models are versioned in the catalog; you can pin and roll out gradually; we also have automatic fallback policies if a model variant degrades. switching involves re-evaluating prompt tokens and potential quantization differences.
[03:48] Samir: audit question: how long are logs retained and can we lengthen retention?
[03:52] Jenna: retention tiers are configurable on enterprise plans — hosted default retention is X days but audit retention add-on increases it. we'll include exact numbers in the security doc.
[04:04] Alice: okay, so next steps — bench, docs, and a quick POC — what about contract/legal?
[04:09] Jenna: for PLG and small pilot it's our standard T&Cs and a simple trial credit agreement. for enterprise we'd go to procurement. since you want pilot in two weeks we can keep it under PLG onboarding first.
[04:20] Priya: can you share the quickstart playbook and an example implementation repo?
[04:24] Marco: yes — we'll share a repo link and a short script to run the bench. i'll include notes about batching, cache, and sequence length tradeoffs.
[04:34] Ben: competitor question — we are also talking with Anthropic and a couple of smaller inference vendors.
[04:39] Jenna: noted, is there anything specific from them you're comparing vs Redwood?
[04:44] Alice: mainly pricing and latency SLAs, plus how easy it is for our engineers to get to a working build.
[04:49] Marco: we aim to be predictable on latency and cost — our Optimize product gives batching/quantization recs for your workload.
[04:58] Priya: okay, let's capture actions.
[05:00] Jenna: recap: we will send quickstart playbook, security pack (SOC2, SAML details, KMS options), perf spreadsheet, and create a bench run on hosted if you send prompts.
[05:10] Samir: i'll own providing a list of EU vs US data residency requirements and a point-of-contact.
[05:14] Ben: i'll send sample prompts and a small eval set by tomorrow.
[05:18] Alice: i'll sync procurement timeline but expect to be ready for pilot sign-off in two weeks.
[05:24] Jenna: awesome. schedule wise, we'll target the bench run to start 2026-06-04 or 06-05 depending on when we get artifacts.
[05:32] Marco: any last questions?
[05:35] Priya: none on my end, thanks.
[05:37] Jenna: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links and docs.
[05:40] (call ends)
